Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings. This meeting will be held via videoconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to the Governor's Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Safer at Home Order (revised March 21, 2020). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will not be livestreamed. You may attend the meeting through a computer or telephone:
BY COMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/87006512022
Zoom Meeting ID: 870 0651 2022
BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code: 870 0651 2022#
HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit email correspondence to CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org before the meeting begins. The email will be distributed to all councilmembers. Public correspondence submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: If you would like to address the City Council during the meeting, please utilize the "Raise Hand" feature during the meeting, or email CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org with (1) the agenda item on which you'd like to speak, and (2) the phone number and/or Zoom display name from which you will be calling in to the meeting. This will replace the in-person speaker cards.

INCORPORATED 1939

  MINUTES
  OF THE APRIL 13, 2021 REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City Council meeting via Zoom
pursuant to Executive Order N25-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom on March 26, 2020,
was called to order by Mayor Kemps at 6:34 P.M. on April 6, 2021 , notice having been given
with affidavit thereto on file. Members of the public were provided with the following
information to provide public input:

  BY COMPUTER: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/87006512022
  Zoom Meeting ID: 870 0651 2022
  BY TELEPHONE: 1669900 9128, Enter Code: 870 0651 2022#
  BY EMAIL: CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org

NEXT RESOLUTION NO. R21-16

NEXT ORDINANCE NO. 021-748

CALL TO ORDER 6:34 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

PRESENT: Mayor Kemps, Mayor Pro Tern Lozzi, Councilmembers McGowan, Roos and
Murdock

ALSO PRESENT:
City Manager Guglielmo, City Attorney Cotti, Treasurer Greenberg, Acting Police Chief Best,
Community Development Director Rindge, City Support Services Director Hannah, City Clerk
Chaney

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Murdock, seconded by Councilmember Roos to approve
the agenda.
AYES: Murdock, Roos, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
NOES: None

MAYOR'S REPORT
Mayor Kemps reported on legislative activity, citing AB 1258. Mayor Kemps also recognized
and provided a tribute in memory of Phil Coyne.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT
City Manager Guglielmo wished Mayor Kemps a Happy Birthday.
Acting Chief Best provided recognition and spoke on the passing of Reserve Officer and DDP
Volunteer John Douglass. He also noted National Public Safety Telecommunicators week
honoring the dispatchers in the department.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Valerie Gorsuch and Desiree Myers addressed the City Council.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

APRIL 13, 2021
 CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1 - 8)

ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tern Lozzi, seconded by Councilmember Murdock to approve
the agenda with the removal of item #6 at the request of Councilmember Roos .
AYES: Murdock, Roos, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
NOES: None

1.  City Council Action Minutes

  Reviewed and Approved:
  a.  March 23, 2021 Special Meeting Minutes
  b.  March 23, 2021 Regular Meeting Minutes

2.  Approval of Warrant Registers

  Reviewed and Approved Warrant Registers.

3.  Approval of an Amended and Restated License Agreement for use of George
  Allen Field with Peninsula Junior League Baseball

  Approved an Amended and Restated License Agreement for Use of George Allen
  Field with Peninsula Junior League Baseball; (2) authorized the City Attorney to
  review/prepare the necessary documents; and (3) authorized the City Manager to
  execute such documents on behalf of the City.

4.  Notice of Vacancies on Commissions and Committees

  Received and Filed.

5.  Adoption of Resolution R21-16 Establishing Compensation and Benefits for the
  Chief of Police

  Adopted Resolution 21-16 establishing the compensation and benefits for the Chief
  of Police.

6.  Removed from Consent Agenda

7.  Acceptance of Donations

  Reviewed and Accepted.

8.  Letter of Support for Assembly Constitutional Amendment (ACA) No. 7 - Local
  Land Use Authority

  Authorized the Mayor to sign a letter of support for ACA (Assembly Constitutional
  Amendment) No. 7 introduced by Assembly Member Muratsuchi.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT AGENDA

6.  Recommendations of the Parklands Committee on March 11, 2021

  Recommendation: Approve the Actions of the Parklands Committee for the meeting of
  March 11 , 2021.

  Barbara Pavliscak and Casey Crowe addressed the City Council.

  The City Council discussed the Parklands Committee actions and the process for City
  Council review and approval, and opted not to assert jurisdiction.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tern Lozzi, seconded by Councilmember McGowan to
  approve the actions of the Parklands Committee for the meeting of March 11, 2021.

 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

APRIL 13, 2021
   AYES: Murdock, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
  NOES: Roos

PUBLIC HEARING(S)/ORDINANCES

9.  Ordinance Amending Chapter 15.50 (Floodplain Management) of Title 15 of the
  Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code

  The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) deadline for adoption of a
  Floodplain Management Ordinance is April 21 , 2021 , requiring that the City Council
  adopt an Emergency Ordinance to take immediate effect. The City Council must also
  adopt a regular Ordinance which, after the normal process which includes a first
  reading, second reading and 30 days, will supersede the Emergency Ordinance.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Murdock, seconded by Councilmember
  McGowan to Adopt Urgency Ordinance No. 021-748U:

  AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES
  ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 15.50 (FLOODPLAIN
  MANAGEMENT) OF TITLE 15 OF THE PALOS VERDES ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE AND FINDING THE ACTION EXEMPT FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  AYES: Murdock, Roos, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
  NOES: None

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Murdock, seconded by Councilmember
  McGowan to Introduce on first reading Ordinance No. 021-749:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA,  AMENDING  CHAPTER  15.50 (FLOODPLAIN
  MANAGEMENT) OF TITLE 15 OF THE PALOS VERDES ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE AND FINDING THE ACTION EXEMPT FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  AYES: Murdock, Roos, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
  NOES: None

CEREMONIAL MATTERS

  •  Swearing-in of Anthony "Tony" Best, Chief of Police

  Mayor Kemps provided an introduction of Chief Best and City Manager Guglielmo
  administered the Oath of Office to swear-in Tony Best as Chief of Police.

  Chief Best provided his comments.

  The following individuals addressed the City Council: Merlin David, Steve Friedrich,
  Laura Agnew, Phil Solomita, Lynn Solomita, and Valerie Gorsuch.

MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

  •  Update from Dr. Cherniss, Superintendent of Schools, Palos Verdes Peninsula
  Unified School District

  Superintendent Dr. Chemiss and Board Member Rick Phillips provided an update on the
  Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District reopening. Dr. Chemiss also recognized
  the passing of Board Member Jeffrey Frankel.

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

APRIL 13, 2021
 10.  Guidelines for Access to Public Records

  The City Clerk explained the intent of developing these guidelines is to document the
  process for the public and staff and to better ensure consistent compliance.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Murdock, seconded by Councilmember Roos
  to adopt the Proposed Guidelines for Access to Public Records.
  AYES: Murdock, Roos, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
  NOES:

11.  Receive and File Communication Detailing Changes to the City's Fund Structure
  as Part of the Fiscal Year 2021-22 Budget Development

  The City Council discussed and asked questions regarding funding and expenditures
  related to the new fund structure, with a focus on the equipment replacement fund.
  The City council received and filed the report of staff regarding changes to the City's
  fund structure as part of the FY 2021-22 budget development.

12.  Authorize the City Manager to Execute a Professional Services Agreement with
  Forum-Info Tech For Information Technology Managed Services in an Amount
  not to Exceed $175,000 Per Fiscal Year for a Base Term of Three Years and
  Three Optional One-Year Extensions

  Desiree Myers addressed the City Council.

  The Director of City Support Services explained the Request for Proposals Process
  and provided updated cost estimates based upon ongoing negotiations.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember McGowan, seconded by Councilmember Roos
  to authorize the City Manager to prepare a professional services agreement with
  Forum-Info Tech (FIT) for Information Technology Managed Services (ITMS) and to
  bring the agreement back to the City Council for review and approval.
  AYES: Murdock, Roos, McGowan, Lozzi, Kemps
  NOES:

13.  Discussion of Pension Funding Policy Considerations

  Desiree Myers addressed the City Council.

  After hearing several options to pay down the existing unfunded accrued pension
  liability (UAL), the City Council identified its long-term goal to responsibly fund
  promised pension benefits while keeping interest costs to a minimum. It identified its
  shorter-term priority to eliminate any new pension debt, defined as no growth in the
  UAL year over year, and to later identify targeted funding level goals.

 MAYOR AND COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS

 Councilmember Murdock congratulated Chief Best and thanked Neighborhood Watch and the
 Police Department. She noted the upcoming application period for the Commission and
 Committee vacancies. She asked for a follow-up from recent Traffic Safety Committee items on
 curb painting and speed monitoring. She requested information on a lower cost solution, such as
 volunteers, for conducting the Tree Inventory. She reported that she attended South Bay Cities
 Council of Governments Steering Committee Meeting and California Alliance of Local Electeds.

 Councilmember Roos congratulated and thanked Chief Best.

 Councilmember McGowan congratulated Chief Best and reported on the Golf Club and Tennis
 Club task force activities. He also provided an update on the litigation between Los Angeles
 County and the Sanitation District.

 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

 APRIL 13, 2021
 Councilmember Lozzi also encouraged residents to apply for committee appointments. She
noted the upcoming Bulky Waste pick up event on April 24, and congratulated Chief Best.

ADJOURNMENT TO TUESDAY, April 27, 2021AT6:30 P.M.

There being no further business before the City Council, the meeting was adjourned at 10:04
p.m.

RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED,

  Michael Kemps, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

APRIL 13, 2021
